races.name: Betfred Flying Scotsman Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Varzi
runners_data.note: Lightly raced K.R. Burke 2yo who has won over 6f on good and placed over the same trip; stepping up to 7f for the first time here is a significant query, and drawn in stall 3 (favoured) he sits in good ground on the map but the trip extension on good-to-soft is unproven.

runners_data.name: Kach Above
runners_data.note: Has won three times over 7f on good ground and looks very much at home on this course and distance profile; David Loughnane's yard is out of recent form (0/20 last 14 days) which is a flag, but this horse's repeated 7f Doncaster-style form is genuinely relevant and he could run into the places.

runners_data.name: Dandyman Dan
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard identifies him as a leading danger; prominent-styled, he has one win from five runs this campaign and his sole similar-going run returned a modest 1/5 in soft — the going is therefore a mild concern — but Oliver Cole has two winners from nine in the past 14 days and Kevin Stott keeps him competitive if the pace suits.

runners_data.name: Engraved
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe runner with just one run to his name — a second over 8f on good — so this is a sharp drop in trip and a significant step up in class to Listed level; the form is very limited but the prominent style from a neutral draw keeps him part of the pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Forbidden Fire
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's sole runner here won over 6f on good last time out and now faces a step up to 7f in Listed company; Oisin Murphy's booking is a big positive, but stall 8 (against) on a course where low draws are favoured means he will need to use energy early to get into position from his wide berth.

runners_data.name: Rock Montreal
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's once-raced winner over 7f on good ground has obvious form relevance at this trip; drawn in stall 7 (against) which is a disadvantage on a day where low draws are favoured, and while the trainer is capable, the wide draw and lack of experience make him an each-way interest at best.

runners_data.name: Nabati
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard top pick at high confidence; Charlie Appleby's OR=104 hold-up type is the classiest runner in the field by rating, William Buick takes the mount, and three runs all on good ground have produced two wins — the good-to-soft is a minor going query but nothing alarming, and stall 4 (neutral) is workable for a horse who will come from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Minkaas
runners_data.note: T.J. Kent's hold-up type arrives from a wide draw in stall 9 (against) with modest form over shorter trips (5-6f) and a very low trainer strike rate recently (0/4 last 14 days); the step up to 7f, the draw, and the class rise into Listed make this a tough ask despite a recent win over 6f on good.

runners_data.name: Vega King
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner drawn ideally in stall 2 (favoured); K.R. Burke's 2yo won over 8f on good last time but his most recent 7f run was a poor 10th, and he set the pace today — if he controls from the front without pressure, he becomes dangerous, but his form profile does not inspire confidence that he can sustain it at Listed level.

races.paceDynamic: Vega King is the sole confirmed front-runner and, drawn in stall 2 (favoured), should establish an uncontested lead from the outset on this flat 7f Doncaster straight, setting a honest but manageable tempo on good-to-soft ground — not a suicidal gallop, but enough to stretch the field. Dandyman Dan (prominent) and Engraved and Forbidden Fire (all prominent-styled) will likely settle in behind the leader in the first two furlongs, creating a compact chasing group rather than any secondary pace battle. With only one genuine pace-setter and no rival to push Vega King wide or hard into the early stages, the tempo should be controlled and even — the kind of rhythm that rewards horses who can travel smoothly into the race and produce a sustained late effort, rather than those needing a truly searching gallop to bring hold-up horses into play. This race shape squarely favours prominent-to-midfield horses with a strong cruising speed who can sit just off a moderate pace and kick: the Strand Scorecard's top pick Nabati, a hold-up type with a smooth high-class turn of foot, is the primary beneficiary if the pace is honest enough to expose the front-runners — but the tactical risk is that Vega King's soft lead gifts the early pacesetter an unearned advantage, which is the principal danger scenario.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Vega King Controls, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Vega King leads at a fair but unforced pace and the prominent horses fail to quicken sufficiently turning into the straight.
scenarios.body: Vega King dictates from stall 2 on a flat track with no pressure, but the steady-enough gallop on good-to-soft gives midfield horses like Nabati and Kach Above enough tempo to organise their challenge; Nabati's high-class cruising speed allows William Buick to travel into contention effortlessly and produce a winning kick in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Vega King Steals It on Easy Lead
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and Vega King is permitted to coast along at the front unchallenged, stealing an unassailable break.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to pressure Vega King early, the leader sets a dawdling fractions that suits his stamina on this flat track, and the closers — including Nabati — find themselves with too much ground to make up in the short straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses into a sprint finish and the horses settled just behind the leader kick first and fastest.
scenarios.body: Dandyman Dan and Forbidden Fire, sitting comfortably in the prominent group, are ideally positioned to pounce on any weakness from Vega King in the closing stages; this scenario suits those who can hold a prominent pitch without burning energy early, which the good-to-soft ground and flat track permits.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Big Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is uncharacteristically strong and the race falls apart for the fancied runners due to traffic or wide draws.
scenarios.body: Rock Montreal or Minkaas, both improving lightly-raced types, could benefit from chaos or a stronger-than-expected gallop stringing out the field and flattening the classier hold-up runners; these are low-probability beneficiaries whose inexperience makes them unlikely to execute unless conditions conspire perfectly.

watchPoints.text: Watch Vega King's early splits — if Clifford Lee sends him clear from stall 2 and nothing follows aggressively, the race shape turns into a stolen-lead scenario that could seriously flatter a horse with modest Listed credentials.

Nabati is drawn in stall 4 (neutral) for a hold-up horse: William Buick will need to find room in the straight and if traffic builds on the low-draw side, his run could be momentarily blocked at a critical point.

Forbidden Fire's wide draw (stall 8, against) means Oisin Murphy will either use energy forcing a position early or accept a disadvantaged wide route — either outcome is a cost on good-to-soft ground over 7f.

Dandyman Dan's only soft-ground run this season yielded a 9th of 9 over 6f — while today's good-to-soft is not as testing, any overnight deterioration in the going would significantly undermine his chances as Strand Scorecard danger.
Kach Above's trainer David Loughnane is 0/20 in the last 14 days — worth monitoring market moves for this runner as a guide to whether the team consider the horse fully tuned for this return.

races.paceDynamic: Clatford and Masaban are both confirmed front-runners drawn 2 and 10 respectively, and their presence guarantees a genuinely contested early gallop — neither is likely to concede the lead without a fight, meaning the pace will be honest rather than manufactured on the soft ground. Bella Bisbee (draw 5, favoured) and Celtic Chariot (draw 1, favoured) will push forward from prominent positions, adding further pressure to the early exchanges and stretching the field through the first half of this mile. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions, with Shadow Run and Feel The Need — both true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map — unlikely to get the truly patient ride they need; Celtic Chariot and Bella Bisbee are better placed by draw to actually land prominent berths. A genuinely run soft-ground mile off a contested pace on a flat track that rewards relaxed midfield travellers who can lengthen through the final two furlongs — prominent horses drawn to the favoured left rail who can settle just off the speed without over-racing hold the clearest structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Rail Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Clatford and Masaban force each other along and the favoured left-rail draw delivers a clear positional edge into the straight.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a strong but honest tempo on soft ground, with the field stringing out early and the favoured low-number draws allowing Celtic Chariot and Bella Bisbee to travel just off the pace in the best ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Pace Test
scenarios.trigger: If Masaban dictates from Clatford and the pace, while genuine, does not fully collapse the leader entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Masaban, the Strand Scorecard top selection, is able to control the tempo and finds enough on soft ground — where the horse has a placed effort — to hold on as closers cannot quite muster sufficient momentum from rear.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early battle between Clatford and Masaban burns both out and the pace genuinely collapses, leaving a clear path for a midfield horse to swoop.
scenarios.body: A strong early tempo on soft ground leaves the front pair vulnerable in the final furlong, and a well-positioned midfield traveller from a neutral draw can pick up the pieces with a sustained run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Punish Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so strong that even midfield horses struggle and genuine hold-up horses get an unusually clean run through from the rear.
scenarios.body: This scenario is structurally discounted because Shadow Run and Feel The Need — the most natural closers — are both redistributed types unlikely to secure the patient position required, making a pure late sweep a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Celtic Chariot drew stall 1 — the most favoured position on this left-biased track — and has won twice at this trip; watch whether Adrian Nicholls commits to the rail from the off, as the draw gives Celtic Chariot a free lane that most rivals cannot access.

Clatford returns from 85 days off for a stable (Scott Dixon, 0/20 in 14 days) and is a confirmed front-runner — if Clatford fades badly in the straight after forcing the pace, this will materially change the winning margin for anything held up behind.

Masaban must navigate from draw 10 (NEUTRAL) to find the favoured left rail — watch the first two furlongs to see whether the horse gets across cleanly or is forced wide, as that positional cost on soft ground could be decisive at this level.

Little Miss India is returning from 140 days off; a hold-up horse over shorter than its recent winning trips — if it moves smoothly in the preliminaries and jockey Gary Bardwell positions handily early, the absence concern is reduced, but watch the markets for any drift.

Wield carries a tongue-tie and recorded a zero (likely pulled-up) on latest run — if the horse moves freely in the parade ring and Joe Fanning settles it quickly from the favoured draw 3, the run may be informative for future handicaps even if the latest effort raised questions.

runners_data.name: Sale Shark
runners_data.note: Won on soft over 5f last time and returns to identical conditions with Oisin Murphy in the saddle; Hugo Palmer's two-year-old sprinters fire fresh, and the inside draw at 1 gives Murphy options to slot into a prominent berth without burning fuel in the early scramble.

runners_data.name: Carry The Flag
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the mount for Aidan O'Brien but this colt's form figures on soft are thin — one run, finishing seventh — and his best efforts have come on good ground over 6f; the step down to 5f on a testing surface is a notable ask.

runners_data.name: In The Black
runners_data.note: Promising winner on good ground over 5f on debut, but its natural style is to race prominently; with the field stacked with pace-hungry types, it is likely to find its usual position crowded out and may have to settle further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Agamemnon
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope's mount has a fair fourth on soft in the book and races in the midfield, giving it a clean run through the melee of prominent horses; Richard Hughes has placed this juvenile well at pattern level before, and the soft 5f here suits its sustained galloping profile.

runners_data.name: Final Objective
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection and one of two confirmed front-runners; James Doyle will aim to find a clear early lead, and the colt's soft-ground second last time out at 6f suggests the shorter trip on similar ground plays to its stamina-backed speed rather than against it.

runners_data.name: Crownbreaker
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy's charge has a placed effort at 5f on good ground and a win at the trip on its CV; it wants a prominent berth but will face fierce competition for position, and the soft seventh at Haydock is a going query that tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Flann Sunna
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride on a filly who has won her last two on good ground at 6f; the step to soft at 5f is the unknown, with 43 days off the track adding a small fitness caveat, but Buick is adept at placing prominent horses on the Doncaster straight and the Crisford yard travels well.

runners_data.name: Tokaido
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, which is an obvious concern in a strongly-run 5f on soft; the sole soft-ground run produced a finish of 16th, and the hold-up style mapped here requires a very specific race scenario to overcome the stamina warning.

runners_data.name: Fast Track
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner with a win at 5f on good ground and multiple placed efforts at the trip; Tom Marquand will push for the early lead, but the contested battle with Final Objective over soft ground risks draining both horses before the final furlong arrives.

runners_data.name: El Floridita
runners_data.note: Visor fitted and races from draw 3 with Rowan Scott; a winner at 5f on good ground and placed on soft, the midfield profile means it avoids the prominent scramble and may find clear air on the nearside as rivals fan; Nigel Tinkler's two-year-olds are consistent performers at this level.

runners_data.name: Pershaada
runners_data.note: OR 106 and placed three times at 5f, but the last run — 14th on soft — is an alarming going flag; Sean Levey will push for a prominent position but a repeat of that soft-ground effort would see it swallowed up before the line.

runners_data.name: Ronson
runners_data.note: A hold-up runner with a win at 5f on good ground but finished 10th on soft last time; Alex Jary takes a rare Group-level ride and the combination of being a true hold-up type in a fast-run 5f sprint and a soft-ground question mark makes this a difficult winning profile to construct.

races.paceDynamic: Final Objective and Fast Track are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested early gallop over 5f on Good To Soft ground — a combination that tends to compress the field and burn off the less resilient speedsters. Sale Shark, Flann Sunna, Carry The Flag, and Pershaada all want to race prominently, meaning the first two furlongs will see a cluster of five or more horses fighting for the same territory, with traffic dangers materialising at the two-furlong pole as the field narrows. Soft-ground stamina and the ability to sustain a strong gallop rather than produce a late burst will be the decisive factor, meaning horses who can track close but controlled — rather than those forced to sprint late from detached positions — are best placed. In The Black is a genuine prominent racer pushed into the midfield mapping because the field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred positions; of the surplus, Sale Shark (inside draw, Murphy) and Flann Sunna (Buick, progressive) are most likely to actually land the prominent spots they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Final Objective and Fast Track fight for the front and a prominent tracker survives the early congestion to collar them late.
scenarios.body: The pace duel between the two front-runners burns energy through soft ground, allowing a well-positioned prominent horse to pick up the pieces inside the final furlong without ever needing a dramatic sprint finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Clearly
scenarios.trigger: If Final Objective or Fast Track shakes off the rival early and establishes a clear, rhythm-controlled lead from the outset.
scenarios.body: A solo leader on soft ground at 5f can control fractions and leave rivals chasing their tails, rewarding the horse that gets its head in front first without expending reserves in a duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stayers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace proves truly punishing and the race degenerates into a stamina test that plays into the hands of midfield finishers.
scenarios.body: Agamemnon or El Floridita, racing off a strong gallop in the belly of the field, find the front two toiling in the final 75 yards and emerge from a bunched finish with reserves intact.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Fliers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so fierce that the entire prominent group ties up, allowing true hold-up horses to scythe through.
scenarios.body: Ronson or Tokaido would need a perfect run through gaps and an unusually dramatic capitulation from the speed, a low-probability chain of events given Tokaido's flagged fade tendency and Ronson's modest recent form.

watchPoints.text: Final Objective and Fast Track will collide for the lead from stalls 8 and 11 — watch whether one folds inside the first furlong or whether a genuine pace duel develops, as that single moment dictates whether this becomes a front-runner's race or a prominent tracker's opportunity.

Prominent congestion is acute: Sale Shark (1), Flann Sunna (2), Pershaada (4), Carry The Flag (12), and Crownbreaker (10) all want the same early real estate — any bumping or checking at the two-furlong marker could compromise multiple fancied runners simultaneously.

Pershaada's 14th-place finish on soft ground last time is the starkest going flag in this field; if conditions ride genuinely soft rather than merely good-to-soft, she is a significant risk to backers despite her 106 rating.

Tokaido is tagged as a horse that fades in the finish — in a contested 5f sprint this is almost certainly a non-starter for winning purposes, but it may cause interference if it weakens rapidly through the field in the closing stages and impedes late-running rivals.

Flann Sunna arrives on 43 days off and on significantly softer ground than her two wins; William Buick's ability to get prominent types into rhythm quickly on the Doncaster straight is the one factor that could paper over those cracks.

runners_data.name: Caballo De Mar
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner with soft-ground form (won at 3f on soft, 1W from 3 sim-going runs) and Ryan Moore-less Oisin Murphy in the plate; wears a hood and has a history of fading in the finish, which is a real concern over 2m2f on soft — controlling the race is its only winning mechanism, and it faces a stamina test it has not demonstrably passed.

runners_data.name: Winday
runners_data.note: William Buick teams up with Emmet Mullins for this lightly-raced three-year-old whose sole win came on good ground over 1m4f — this horse's natural instinct is to press the pace, but the field configuration means it is unlikely to get that berth, and racing in an uncharacteristically restrained role may blunt its effectiveness; the step to 2m2f on soft is a significant unknown.

runners_data.name: Queenstown
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this six-year-old who landed his last win over 1m6f on good and has placed on similar ground twice in five soft-going runs — an established prominent racer who is already mapped to a position that suits his style, and the combination of Ballydoyle class and Moore's judgement of pace makes him the most straightforward profile for the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Epic Poet
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old midfield specialist trained by David O'Meara whose recent form figures (534650) tell a story of gradual decline; one placing from five similar-going runs and a flat effort last time out on soft suggest this trip and conditions are not unlocking his best, though he stays well and Tudhope is capable of conjuring something from an unpromising position.

runners_data.name: Peace Belle
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for Jennie Candlish whose soft-ground record includes a win (2nd from 3 in similar going) and whose last run was a placed effort on soft — the longer she is held up the more reliant she is on a true pace being set, and in a race where tempo may be modest, she could find herself with too much ground to make up, though her stamina profile at 2m2f on soft is a genuine asset.

runners_data.name: Beylerbeyi
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' six-year-old is a hold-up type wearing a hood and a tongue-tie, and his form figures on soft (5th, 10th, 4th from five similar-going runs) suggest he finds soft conditions acceptable but not transformative; Clifford Lee takes the ride and this horse has never won beyond a mile, making the stamina test over 2m2f the primary concern regardless of pace shape.

runners_data.name: Ascending
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old who is naturally inclined to race prominently but whose place in this race is being pushed back by stronger pace rivals — his fades-in-finish flag combined with a poor sim-going record (2/5, 0W) and declining form figures (6-7064) make it hard to build a winning case even if the scenario goes his way; Henry De Bromhead's stable has been in decent form but the raw evidence here is thin.

runners_data.name: Berkshire Sundance
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's six-year-old has won twice on Polytrack over 1m6f (standard ground) and returns here after 42 days off, a noticeable absence — his prominent style maps naturally to the expected race shape, and he has form over 2m2f, but his soft-turf profile is unproven and the layoff combined with an OR of 102 in a Group 2 field raises fitness and class questions.

races.paceDynamic: Caballo De Mar is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead early over 2m2f on soft ground, is set to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled tempo from the front. Berkshire Sundance and Queenstown are both prominent-style horses capable of tracking close to the pace, giving the race a recognisable shape: a led race with a small group of chasers and the hold-up pair of Peace Belle and Beylerbeyi detached at the rear. On soft ground over this stamina-testing trip, a steady-to-moderate gallop with Caballo De Mar dictating sets up a race that will be won by a horse with the class to pick off the leader in the straight rather than one relying on a late surge from far back. The field carries more prominent/front-running intent than the race can accommodate: Winday and Ascending are both genuine pressing types but have been redistributed to midfield because Caballo De Mar and Berkshire Sundance are better placed to hold those lead-adjacent positions, meaning Winday and Ascending will likely race in an unnatural, more restrained role. The race shape therefore strongly favours prominent-to-tracking runners with proven stamina on soft ground and the ability to sustain a long galloping challenge — a profile that suits Queenstown and Berkshire Sundance.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Class Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Caballo De Mar dictates a steady soft-ground gallop and the prominent chasers simply outclass the leader in the straight.
scenarios.body: Caballo De Mar sets fractions that suit a grinding contest rather than a sprint finish, and a horse tracking within two lengths off the lead has all the time to produce a quality late effort on the run-in; the soft ground filters out anything short of genuine stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On Gamely
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and Caballo De Mar gets an uncontested breather, stealing enough margin to hold off challengers.
scenarios.body: A very slowly-run race with minimal pressure would allow Caballo De Mar to conserve energy and quicken away again when challenged in the final two furlongs; horses tracking too close without the lead would find this scenario removes their attacking angle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the prominent group burn each other out, leaving a gap for late closers.
scenarios.body: A scenario where Queenstown or Berkshire Sundance push on earlier than planned drags the race into a lung-testing finish on softground, and the hold-up horses who have been conserving energy get a clean run to cut them down; Peace Belle's soft-ground form is the most relevant profile here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Winday or Ascending break smartly and force a contested pace despite their mapped positions.
scenarios.body: Both horses are natural front-runners pushed into midfield roles and if either refuses to settle and surges forward, the pace lifts sharply from an early stage; this scenario burns off the stamina of the field and paradoxically opens the door for the classiest stayer to pick up the pieces, but is a low-probability shape given jockey instruction and the trip.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Winday or Ascending break sharply from the stalls — if either forces their way to a prominent position against their mapped role, the early pace will be materially faster and will compress the finishing fractions for all hold-up horses.

Caballo De Mar's fade-in-finish flag is critical over this trip on soft: if Queenstown or Berkshire Sundance move upsides before the two-furlong pole rather than waiting for the final furlong, they risk the leader fighting back and the pair burning each other out.

Berkshire Sundance's 42-day absence on return to soft turf after winning on artificial surfaces is a significant fitness angle — watch for how quickly P J McDonald settles and whether the horse travels with its usual fluency in the early stages.

Peace Belle's chance is almost entirely conditional on pace: if Caballo De Mar is allowed a dawdle, the hold-up horses have insufficient run to close, and Jason Hart will need to make a much earlier move than is natural for this filly's style.

The going report shows the 2m2f contest is among the heavier conditions on the card (confirmed soft rather than good-to-soft elsewhere) — any runner with a going preference leaning toward good ground, particularly Epic Poet (15th on soft last time), should be monitored for early signs of discomfort in the going.

runners_data.name: Silver Lake
runners_data.note: Powerful hold-up filly in excellent form (three consecutive wins at 10f on good and soft), stepping up to 1m4f for William Haggas and James Doyle — the extra distance looks tailor-made, and soft ground has never stopped her; draws stall 9 which is neutral at Doncaster but suits a horse who travels wide late.

runners_data.name: Salamanca City
runners_data.note: Five-year-old mare with a strong record at 12f on soft going (three runs, one win two places), well placed by James Fanshawe to exploit a mark of 91; Daniel Muscutt takes over in the saddle and the positive draw in stall 5 suits a horse happy to travel mid-pack.

runners_data.name: Green Sky
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard selection at medium confidence — a six-year-old hold-up mare whose last run was a close third at 12f on soft, with four wins in her last eight starts; Rod Millman's charge has strong course-distance profile and Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim brings her in at a competitive weight.

runners_data.name: Room Fourteen
runners_data.note: Scorecard danger — James Fanshawe's lightly-raced three-year-old has an excellent recent record at 10f on good ground (three wins from five attempts at that trip) but steps up to 1m4f for the first time, which is the one question mark; Saffie Osborne rides, and soft ground has not been tested so connections will be hopeful the stamina and ground both suit.

runners_data.name: Ruby Wedding
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's three-year-old won at 12f on good ground last time and is prominently raced, likely to sit just behind the two front-runners; Oisin Murphy is a formidable booking and if the pace is moderate she could turn stalker, but a win record on soft is absent from her history — stamina here is implied rather than proven.

runners_data.name: Thatwilldoso
runners_data.note: Scorecard danger — prominently raced five-year-old who has won over 10f on good ground twice in recent starts and placed at 12f; her soft-ground record is a concern (10th of 12 at 12f soft last season), which is the main caveat against her figuring prominently if the ground rides genuinely testing.

runners_data.name: Nochebuena
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Ralph Beckett, returning after 63 days off; she won at 12f on soft ground last time out which is a key credential, and if she can establish the lead alone she becomes a real player, but contesting the pace with Golden Muse over 1m4f on soft represents a significant stamina challenge.

runners_data.name: Aequitas
runners_data.note: Long-absent four-year-old (307 days off since a heavy defeat at Chelmsford and a poor Lingfield run), whose sole turf win was at 12f on good; connections have a difficult task asking her to recapture form after such a lay-off, and her reappearance profile makes her the most speculative runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Golden Muse
runners_data.note: The other confirmed front-runner, trained by Marco Botti — her wins have all come on standard-to-fast surfaces at All-Weather tracks, and soft turf at Doncaster over 1m4f represents a sharp gear change; David Egan will push for the early advantage, but her going profile is a genuine concern on a day when the ground is softening.

runners_data.name: Bint Al Daar
runners_data.note: Six-year-old mare rated just 70 whose recent form figures (1-5-8-7-9-0) tell a story of steep decline; Joanna Mason takes the ride and the soft-ground record is poor (11th at 10f soft last time out), making her a difficult selection to support under any scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Nochebuena and Golden Muse are both confirmed front-runners, and with two genuine lead-seeking fillies in a 10-runner field, the early exchanges will be contested — neither is likely to concede the rail without a fight, and that friction will inject honest early tempo into a 1m4f trip on Good To Soft ground at Doncaster. The gallop will be genuine rather than dawdling, and with the mile-and-a-half trip stretching stamina on a softened surface, the pace set by Nochebuena and Golden Muse is likely to be self-defeating for at least one of them, creating a strong tailwind for horses travelling behind the pace. This race shape — a genuine early pace contested between two front-runners on a stamina-testing trip — is a textbook setup for hold-up and midfield horses to close powerfully through the final quarter-mile, rewarding those with proven stamina and the ability to sustain their run in softer ground. The profile that benefits most is a patient hold-up or midfield runner with genuine soft-ground credentials and a proven staying trip, who can be delivered with one sweeping challenge once the pace collapses in the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If Nochebuena and Golden Muse fight for the lead and burn each other out, setting a genuinely strong gallop on softening ground.
scenarios.body: The honest early pace fragments the field, with the two leaders tying each other up through the middle stages before both weakening past the two-furlong pole; hold-up and midfield horses with proven stamina find the race coming to them in the straight, and those with soft-ground form hit the line hardest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Muse or Nochebuena establishes a clear advantage early and the other capitulates, allowing a solo controlled gallop.
scenarios.body: With only one pace-setter dictating at a measured clip, the tempo is less punishing and the leader can conserve enough energy to fight back in the straight; a prominent player who tracks closely in second or third without getting embroiled benefits enormously from the reduced war of attrition.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong but the hold-up horses fail to quicken on the softened surface, allowing a close-tracking prominent racer to win the staying battle.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting third or fourth throughout absorbs the early pace without burning energy fighting for position, and as the leaders weaken the stalker finds just enough to repel the late finishers; soft-ground stamina and a clean position off the pace are the decisive factors here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfielders Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so frenetic that the front two blow up dramatically, leaving the race wide open for a wave of midfield finishers.
scenarios.body: The home straight becomes a free-for-all as the leaders fold and every midfield horse arrives simultaneously, making the race a lottery decided by who picks the clearest passage and who sustains their run longest on the soft surface.

watchPoints.text: Nochebuena and Golden Muse — watch the opening furlong closely: if both press hard for the lead the pace will be genuinely punishing, which radically improves the prospects of hold-up horses Silver Lake and Green Sky.

Golden Muse's going — all her wins are on standard All-Weather surfaces, and if the ground rides closer to Soft than Good To Soft her ability to sustain the front-running role is seriously in doubt, which could cause her to capitulate earlier than expected.

Room Fourteen's trip — she has never raced beyond 10f and this is her first attempt at 1m4f; if she fails to settle in her midfield position the extra distance could find her out, but if she relaxes James Fanshawe's filly has the raw ability to make the step up.

Aequitas — 307 days off the track is the longest absence in the field, and although David O'Meara's stable is in reasonable form, watch for signs of greenness or ring-rustiness in the parade ring and early stages that could mark her as one to oppose.

Green Sky's claim — Charlie Tucker's 7lb allowance is a live factor that materially reduces her burden; watch whether the weight advantage is reflected in market moves closer to post time as a guide to stable confidence.

runners_data.name: It Dunt Marra
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed twice in four starts but is 0-from-4 in similar going; the step up to 6f at Doncaster is new ground and connections must hope his recent 9th on soft does not reflect a real going concern.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Toledo
runners_data.note: Bold front-runner (OR 85) with P J McDonald in the plate — the likeliest candidate to control this race from the front if the chaos of the initial stages can be navigated; one win from three starts and consistent at this level.

runners_data.name: Bear Lee
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator drawn in stall 1 for Joanna Mason and the Easterbys — gets a wide variety of pace to aim at from the rear, and his one win came at 5f on good ground, so this soft 6f tests his stamina reserves more than it might appear from his form.

runners_data.name: Washington Royale
runners_data.note: Already has a win over C&D on soft going (1/6f/SOF), making him arguably the best-credentialled horse in the field for today's conditions; Michael Appleby is well in form (T14: 3/26) and Clifford Lee will look to get a prominent position from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Baddaddan
runners_data.note: Promising sort who won at 6f on good and is stepping back to that trip after a disappointing 14th last time; Richard Spencer's yard is only 3/12 in the past 14 days so form is middling, and this is a big ask on unfamiliar softer ground.

runners_data.name: Super Tuscan
runners_data.note: Consistent enough — two wins and placed form — but all best efforts have come on good or firmer; Eve Johnson Houghton's runner drops back to 6f with an apprentice (Carmichael 7lbs) and will need to prove soft ground is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Henley On Thames
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection at medium confidence — Kevin Philippart De Foy's improving 2yo has won his last two starts and the form has been building nicely; David Egan takes the ride and the horse's prominent style is well suited to tracking a strong gallop and striking late.

runners_data.name: Launch Sequence
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke is flying (T14: 13/42) and James Doyle rides a horse who has been placed twice from three starts; rated OR 85 and mapped to midfield, a headgear note (hg:p) is flagged — if the cheekpieces sharpen his focus he could be a factor from a good draw in stall 7.

runners_data.name: Tumishi
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's prominent racer won most recently over C&D on good ground and has been placed in both prior runs; Daniel Muscutt gets the ride from stall 2 — needs soft ground not to blunt the sharp turn of foot that has carried him into the frame.

runners_data.name: Wait Geordie
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner from stall 5 with a deteriorating form string (138785) — the recent moderate efforts suggest he may lack the class to match his earlier runs, and on soft ground over 6f he is more likely to fade than to dominate.

runners_data.name: Beresford Gap
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy is always a booking that commands respect, and Beresford Gap has placed at 6f on standard — a 50-day break is a notable concern however, and this horse has never won on soft or yielding ground.

runners_data.name: Sir Sirius
runners_data.note: Confirmed lead horse drawn wide in 13 for Kevin Ryan — has been off 78 days which is a significant flag, and his recent form of 963 does not inspire confidence that he can set a useful pace rather than a damaging one.

runners_data.name: Innichen
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides one of the most experienced horses in the field (6 runs) who has two wins at 5f and a 19th last time out on soft that is best ignored; on good ground he is a genuine threat from off the pace, but that alarming soft-going return tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Sue's Last Chance
runners_data.note: A front-runner at the bottom of the handicap (OR 72) with a headgear note (hg:p) — the recent form figures include an 18th and an 8th, so while she adds to the early pace she is unlikely to sustain it, and Richard Fahey's barn has been very busy (T14: 8/66).

runners_data.name: Fasthope
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's runner is a genuine prominent type whose natural style cannot be accommodated in this pace-heavy field — she is likely to find herself raced deeper than ideal, which tempers what looked like a live each-way claim; her one win came over C&D on good ground.

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.note: Duran Fentiman rides a Tim Easterby runner who has won at 6f on good ground and whose form string shows admirable consistency in placing; however, as a true prominent racer pushed back into a midfield role by the sheer volume of pace in this field, she is operating out of her comfort zone and that reduces her winning prospects.

races.paceDynamic: Five confirmed front-runners — Pride Of Toledo, Wait Geordie, Beresford Gap, Sir Sirius, and Sue's Last Chance — will ensure this 6f nursery is run at a fierce gallop from the outset on Good To Soft ground, with no prospect of a false pace or tactical crawl. The early scramble for position will burn through the field's speed reserves quickly, meaning the race will be decided on stamina and the ability to sustain momentum through the final two furlongs rather than on a late sprint. Fasthope and Fern Clyde are genuine prominent-running types who will find themselves unable to secure their natural berth with this many pace horses ahead of them, and are likely to be forced wider and deeper in traffic than suits their profiles. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel powerfully in a prominent-to-midfield position without burning energy in the early stages, switching into the slipstream of the early pace battle and unleashing their effort from two furlongs out — patient, well-positioned stalkers with proven stamina are the profile to follow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, stalkers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the five front-runners burn each other out through a frantic early gallop and begin to fade from halfway, setting up a race won by a horse tracking the pace at a comfortable clip.
scenarios.body: The sustained early pressure on Good To Soft will drain the speed horses in the final furlong, rewarding those who conserved energy in the first half; Henley On Thames, rated OR 83 with a strong recent record of two wins and consistent placing, is ideally suited to tracking a strong pace and picking off weakening leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One leader dictates, stays on
scenarios.trigger: If Pride Of Toledo breaks cleanly, assumes a controlled lead at the head of the pack, and manages to keep rivals at bay while others fight around him.
scenarios.body: Pride Of Toledo has the class (OR 85) and experience over C&D in soft conditions to control the race from the front if the other pace horses become disorganised early; a measured gallop could allow him to conserve enough to hold on up the straight with P J McDonald guiding him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses deliver late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so extreme that it leaves a clear, wide-open track for hold-up horses to produce a sustained late run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Bear Lee and Innichen both operate from off the pace and could benefit if the race turns into a true stamina test over the final two furlongs on tiring ground; Innichen in particular holds an OR of 85 and has shown the ability to finish powerfully from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos favours big-priced runner
scenarios.trigger: If the early scramble for position causes interference, blocked runs, and positional disruption that unsettles the fancied horses and opens the race up for a lower-rated runner.
scenarios.body: Washington Royale (OR 75) has already won over C&D in soft going, giving her a genuine each-way claim if the race degenerates into a scrappy, strung-out affair; Fasthope, though likely raced out of her natural prominent role, has pace figures that could carry her into contention in an untidy race.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Pride Of Toledo or Wait Geordie takes up the true lead early — if they clash from the off the pace will be searingly fast, which could collapse the front entirely and hand the race to a Henley On Thames-style tracker.

Bear Lee is drawn in stall 1 and operates as a hold-up horse — in a 16-runner field with a fierce pace he could find himself trapped against the rail in the early stages; Joanna Mason will need to manage the position carefully.

Sir Sirius has been off 78 days and is one of the confirmed front-runners — a rustiness-inspired wide early move from stall 13 could add to positional chaos and affect the runs of Innichen (stall 11) and Henley On Thames (stall 12).

Fern Clyde and Fasthope are both natural prominent types who cannot get their position — monitor whether either horse's jockey attempts to push forward aggressively from stalls 15/16, as a wide early move could cost ground on soft ground before the race has truly begun.

Launch Sequence carries the headgear flag (cheekpieces) which is worth noting — K.R. Burke's explosive 14-day strike rate (13/42) suggests the yard is in exceptional form, and if the headgear produces the desired response James Doyle from a central draw could make this interesting late.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Olly, Director's Cut, On The Inlet, Canvas, and Ziata all want to be on or near the lead, meaning five legitimate front-runners will contest position from the jump over 1m2f on Good to Soft ground at Doncaster's flat, galloping track. With no single dominant pace-setter able to dictate uncontested, the early stages will be a genuine fight for supremacy, forcing a strong and honest gallop that will stretch the field out significantly by halfway. The soft conditions will compound the stamina test, meaning horses who expend energy scrapping for early position are likely to be vulnerable in the final two furlongs. This race shape clearly favours hold-up and midfield horses who can settle, travel into the race from off the pace, and produce sustained late runs — particularly those with proven soft-ground form and the class to pick off tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace burns off the five front-runners and the race develops into a true stamina test in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: With five horses fighting for the lead on soft ground over 1m2f, the pace will be genuine and unrelenting, leaving closers with ample cover and a slowly weakening pack to pick through; those who settle best and have proven soft-ground stamina will hit the line strongest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-style runners secures a comfortable stalking position just off the contested lead without burning too much fuel.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting second or third early — shielded from the brawl at the front but travelling within range — could inherit the lead as the pace-setters crack entering the final furlong; Everyoneknowsadave or Amancio, both suited by this trip and going, could capitalise from a well-judged stalking ride.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn each other out so completely that the race becomes a mass sprint from two furlongs out and midfield traffic is bypassed by a wider ranker.
scenarios.body: Optician — the Strand Scorecard selection — has proven soft-ground form over this exact trip and, mapping to midfield, could find an uncongested path wide of tired rivals; Almekarem also has course-relevant form and carries midfield credentials that suit a late wave.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters — most likely Director's Cut or On The Inlet — establishes a clear early lead rather than scrapping with rivals and is allowed a soft enough gallop to conserve energy.
scenarios.body: Though unlikely given five rivals competing for the front, a horse that breaks cleanly and finds itself briefly alone on the rail could set a controlled pace and prove difficult to peg back in the closing stages; Director's Cut has won from the front before and Ross Burdon's runner will be ridden to exploit any early split.

watchPoints.text: Five front-runners — Highland Olly, Director's Cut, On The Inlet, Canvas, and Ziata — are all drawn between 7 and 18 and will collide at the break; watch for any one of them to be knocked sideways or forced wide as they fight for rail position, because a clean passage could be the difference between finishing and fading.

Fans Favourite is ridden by Oisin Murphy — a significant jockey booking drop into a competitive handicap — and if Murphy gets a dream run from the hold-up position as the pace implodes, this three-year-old's soft-ground record makes him dangerous regardless of starting price.

Optician's Strand Scorecard selection is flagged low confidence, and the horse's last win on soft at 1m2f was some time ago; if the pace somehow moderates (unlikely with five front-runners) and the race is not truly run, the midfield position could leave the horse with too much to do.

Something Splendid — the Strand Scorecard danger — is drawn in stall 2 and Tom Marquand must decide immediately whether to push forward to a prominent position or drop in; from the lowest draw in a race where inside ground on soft should theoretically be advantageous, the opening two furlongs will define this horse's race.

Reveur's going is marked unknown and the horse is 126 days off the track as a lightly-raced three-year-old — if Daniel Tudhope produces a big run fresh it would be an eyecatcher, but punters should note the risk before committing on this runner's chance in genuinely testing conditions.
